reason: The flora says 'Fruit ellipsoid, 10-15 mm long'. Fruit length 10–15 mm is right.
'Suborbicular' means almost orbicular, so orbicular marked 'approximately' fits. These are the bracts of the male spike, and the statement is true of them.

fix: Check ranges where the upper end is more than about 10 times the lower end; they are often a lost decimal point in the source (1.1 printed as 11).
reason: The annotation copies the text, but an 11 mm style is not possible in a Hydrocotyle flower with 1 mm bracts and a 1.3 mm fruit. The source almost surely means 0.7–1.1 mm.

fix: In Apiaceae and other umbel descriptions, 'rays' are the stalks of the compound umbel, which are primary inflorescence branches, not ray flowers. Read 'rays' as ray flowers only in Asteraceae head contexts (ray florets, ligules).
reason: The Daucus rays are 3–7.5 cm long and 'compact in fruit'. They are umbel branches, not ray flowers.

fix: 'crisped pilose' / 'crisped-pilose' should map to pilose (crisped hairs), not to the generic pubescent hair.
reason: The flora says pilose, and FLOPO has a pilose value class. The bearer (stem, upper part) is right.
Leaves shorter than the culm: decreased length relative to the stem (culm) is right.

fix: In a gamosepalous calyx ('Calyx campanulate ...; lobes ...'), 'lobes' means calyx lobes, not sepals. Use the calyx lobe class when the lobes belong to a calyx tube.
reason: The calyx is campanulate and the lobes are only 1.5–2 mm. The shapes describe the calyx lobes.

fix: Leading 'in male' / 'in female' qualifiers must fill the sex slot (male: PATO_0000384).
reason: Male inflorescences are 2–3 cm and female ones 1–2 cm long. Without the sex, the 2–3 cm length is false for the female plant.

fix: When 'base' follows a 'leaf blade' clause (separated by ';'), the outer bearer is the leaf blade, so 'base' means the leaf lamina base, not the leaf base (the petiole insertion).
reason: The cuneate base belongs to the blade: 'leaf blade ... ovate or elliptic; base broadly cuneate; apex rounded'.
Pistils longer than stamens. This follows the accepted rule pistil → gynoecium (C253). In this apocarpous Rubus each pistil is strictly a carpel, but the comparison still holds.
'Inflorescence ... apical' means the inflorescence is terminal.
The pedicel is 'pubérulent puis ± glabrescent' (hairy, then nearly hairless). Glabrescent marked 'approximately' fits, and glabrescent already implies the change with age.
'Bracts whitish' is white marked 'approximately', on the bract.
'Never aculeate' is the negation of spiny, by the accepted rule aculeate → spiny (C307). 'Never' covers every age, so leaving out 'young' does not make it false.

fix: In 'Leaves basal (X) and cauline', a parenthetical right after 'basal' qualifies only the basal leaves.
reason: Only the basal leaves are 'not persistent'. Said of all leaves, the statement also covers the cauline leaves, which the flora does not say.
'blade ... base cuneate': leaf lamina base cuneate is right.

fix: 'spreading to N m' gives the spread (lateral extent) of the plant, not its height.
reason: Agelanthus is a mistletoe that spreads over its host. 'Spreading to 1 m' is its spread, not its height.
The leaflets are glabrous on the upper (adaxial) side. Leaf adaxial epidermis is a general class that covers the leaflet surface.

fix: In 'bracteal leaves with petiole ...', the petiole belongs to the leafy bracts. The whole slot must hold the bract, not the leaf by default.
reason: The 1.5–3 mm petiole belongs to the bracteal leaves in the cyme, not to the main leaves.
'Both stellate-pubescent' covers the peduncles. The pedicels should get a second annotation. The stellate hair type is lost, but the annotation is not false.
Carex has 4–12 spikes: the count of spike inflorescences is right.

fix: A surface word ('abaxial surface') takes the nearest part named in the same clause (here 'peduncular bract') as its outer bearer, not the leaf by default.
reason: The dense red-brown tomentum is on the abaxial surface of the peduncular bract, not on a leaf.

fix: Adverbs such as 'abaxially' / 'adaxially' before a quality must narrow the bearer to that surface.
reason: Only the abaxial side is ± tomentose; the adaxial side is glabrous. Said of the whole blade, the statement is false.
The stamens are slightly shorter than the corolla tube: decreased length relative to the corolla tube is right.
'Leaflets ... oblong in shape' is right.
Young twigs become glabrous with age: stem glabrous in the 'old' context (PATO_0000308) is right.
'Lorate' means strap-shaped.
The leaf blade margin has 1 basal gland per side. Glands as secretory tissue, the count of 1 per side, and the leaf blade as container are acceptable.

fix: In 'Inflorescence a panicle, branches not whorled', 'branches' means inflorescence branches. The quality belongs to them, not to the inflorescence as a whole.
reason: 'Not whorled' describes how the panicle branches are arranged.
Trunk diameter up to 3 dm is up to 30 cm, and the trunk is a stem. The unit is converted correctly.
